name: Feature cards with inset panels
for: The features grid of a product page, as on the best company sites: a centred headline and a grey line, then a 2x2 of cards, each a title and two grey lines, then an inset panel with its own margin holding a bright painterly or grain ground and one smaller UI window that runs out through the panel's bottom edge. Two panels run a short pointer demo; the cards never move.
how: Each panel names its ground in data-cx-effect, its light in data-cx-scene (day, dusk or meadow, for painterly-landscape) and its composition in data-cx-params (horizon, side, slope), so no two panels look alike. The grounds are still: drawn once as they near the screen, kept as pictures and their WebGL context freed, one after another, so the cards hold no context and draw no frames at rest. A landscape takes a natural light near the page: a pale sky over graphite hills under a warm accent, blue-grey under a cool one, the accent itself when it is green or neutral, the page colour's own shades on a colour page; dusk is a deep blue evening sky lit in gold along the horizon, whatever the accent (a blue glow read as the day panel again); meadow is natural daylight (a blue sky over sunlit grass), as a photograph would show it. The sample grid mixes day, a grain, dusk and meadow. The window is plain HTML in the page's own ground colour, cut by the panel's bottom edge (classes --bleed, --narrow, --side vary its width and place); its content runs out through that edge. A card is a subgrid of two rows, so the text zones of a row share one height. Panels with data-cx-loop run a pointer demo (glide, click, state change, rest) only while on screen, each with a pause button in its top-right corner.
rules: Text only in the top zone on the flat card fill; the panel never reaches under it.
Panel margin 8px on three sides, panel radius = card radius - margin.
Every window runs out through the panel's bottom edge; never a small dialog centred on an empty ground (that reads cheap).
No orb, sphere or other focal ground in these panels: the window is the subject.
One capability per card, one UI window per panel, real labels in it (never lorem), no UI text under 11px.
At most two looping panels in view (one per row); the others show a settled still.
The loop never follows scroll and the card never moves.
Every panel a different picture: a different scene or composition, or a grain; never four copies of one landscape, never a landscape painted in the accent hue only.
The window's content reaches the panel's bottom edge: no empty band under its last row.
a11y: Each card has a heading and a sentence that say what the feature does; the UI windows are illustrations (aria-hidden). Looping panels have a pause button; reduced motion shows the end state with no pointer and no button.
